name: rule-based-system
context: Systems requiring explicit, auditable decision logic where expert knowledge is codifiable and explainability is mandatory
benefits: Complete explainability with traceable rule firing history
Regulatory auditability through explicit decision paths
No training data required: knowledge from domain experts
Declarative IF-THEN rules intuitive for domain experts
tradeoffs: Knowledge acquisition bottleneck: domain expert elicitation is time-consuming
Scalability limits with large rule sets (10,000+ rules show non-linear conflict growth)
Brittleness with complex domains: rule interactions become unpredictable
Maintenance complexity at scale requires dedicated tooling
Rule authoring requires specialized knowledge engineering skills
use_cases: Clinical decision support and treatment validation
Workflow orchestration based on business conditions
Fraud detection thresholds and risk parameters
avoid_when: Training data is abundant and patterns are statistical
Domain experts cannot reach consensus on solution approach
Patterns too complex for explicit rule authoring
Probabilistic reasoning or uncertainty handling required
Low-latency real-time scoring at extreme scale
component_types: RuleBase: Collection of IF-THEN production rules representing domain knowledge; organized into modules, packages, or functional clusters; scales to 5,000+ rules in clinical deployments
WorkingMemory: Dynamic store of current facts, asserted data, intermediate conclusions; populated at runtime; volatile between sessions
InferenceEngine: Executes match-resolve-act cycle: (1) Match conditions against facts, (2) Select rule via conflict resolution, (3) Execute and update working memory
UserInterface: Receives input signals, presents conclusions/actions to user
ExplanationModule: Translates rule firing history into natural language; generates audit trails
KnowledgeEngineeringTool: IDE for authoring, testing, and debugging rules
Agenda: Manages execution order of conflicting rules using selected resolution strategy
PatternMatcher: Compares rule antecedents against working memory contents (often via RETE algorithm)
anti_patterns: Monolithic rule soup: hundreds of unrelated rules in one flat pool with no modular organization
Strongly coupled rules: rules that depend on each other's firing order, making changes unpredictable
Knowledge-acquisition bypass: developers writing rules without domain expert review
Rule proliferation: uncontrolled rule growth without periodic consolidation or retirement
Missing audit trail: rule firings not logged, breaking explainability and compliance
design_principles: Knowledge Separation: Separate domain knowledge (rules) from inference engine logic
Declarative Rules: Express business rules in IF-THEN format without encoding control flow
Explicit Conflict Resolution: Define clear salience/specificity strategies before authoring rules
Modular Organization: Partition rules by functional area; avoid flat rule pools exceeding 1,000 rules
Audit Trail Mandatory: Log every rule firing with timestamp, context, and version for compliance
Version Control Rules: Treat rule files as code; require peer review for all changes
Domain Expert Involvement: Knowledge engineering must involve domain experts, not just developers
Rule Authoring Standards: Establish naming conventions, documentation requirements, and style guides
Conflict Detection: Use tooling to detect subsumption, redundancy, and contradictions before deployment
best_practices: Start With a Bounded Rule Set: pilot with 50-200 high-value rules before scaling to thousands
Modularize by Business Function: partition rules into packages (e.g., eligibility, pricing, compliance) with clear owners
Use a Rule Repository With Version Control: treat rule changes like code changes: review, test, and release them
Write Rules in Domain Language: author rules so domain experts can read and validate them without developer translation
Test Rules Against Golden Cases: maintain a regression suite of input/fact scenarios with expected decisions for every release
Log Every Firing With Context: capture rule version, input facts, and outcome to support audit and dispute resolution
Plan the RETE Capacity Envelope: benchmark conflict-resolution performance at 2-3x expected fact volumes before go-live
Retire Rules Deliberately: schedule periodic reviews to remove obsolete rules instead of letting the knowledge base accrete
